article.title: Dobles modales dialectales
article.part: Registro, variación y norma — Register, variation, and standard usage
article.chapter: Variedades del inglés — Varieties of English

claims.summary: Dialectal double modals such as might could place two modal auxiliaries together as a systematic construction in some varieties of English, notably Southern United States English and attested Scottish varieties. Edited Standard English generally avoids modal stacking and often uses a paraphrase such as might be able to. These forms reflect differences in dialect grammar rather than a universal grammatical deficiency.

links.notes: Huddleston & Pullum (2005) is an active Tier B general English-grammar reference for modal syntax and standard-versus-dialectal contrasts. Specialist corroboration of double modals: Nagle (1994), The English Double Modal Conspiracy, doi:10.1075/dia.11.2.04nag (specialist source not yet separately linked in registry).
